title.en: Linear regression: the loss, the closed form, and gradient descent
title.zh: 线性回归：损失、闭式解与梯度下降

description.en: The linear model and its squared-error loss, the normal equation derived by matrix calculus, least squares as maximum likelihood under Gaussian noise, gradient descent versus the closed form, and how to judge a fit.
description.zh: 线性模型与平方误差损失，用矩阵微积分推出正规方程，最小二乘即高斯噪声下的最大似然，梯度下降与闭式解的对比，以及怎样评判拟合。

name.en: The linear model and its assumptions
Squared-error loss and optimisation by derivatives
name.zh: 平方误差损失与用导数优化

name.en: Gradient descent and the learning rate
Strengths and weaknesses of linear regression

description.en: Trusting a linear fit outside the range of the training features
description.zh: 在训练特征范围之外信任线性拟合

description.en: Thinking a larger learning rate always converges faster
description.zh: 以为学习率越大收敛越快

description.en: Thinking squared error makes no assumption about the noise
description.zh: 以为平方误差对噪声没有任何假设

description.en: Ignoring correlated features when using the normal equation
description.zh: 用正规方程时忽视相关特征

title.en: The model: a line (or hyperplane) through the data
title.zh: 模型：穿过数据的一条线（或超平面）

text.en: Regression predicts a **number**. Linear regression assumes the target is a weighted sum of the features plus a constant, so the data are summarised by a line in 2D and a hyperplane in higher dimensions. The deck predicts income (thousand dollars) from hours worked per week:
text.zh: 回归预测的是一个**数**。线性回归假设目标等于各特征的加权和再加一个常数，所以数据被概括成二维里的一条直线、更高维里的一个超平面。课件用每周工时来预测收入（千美元）：

items.zh: $y$：**目标**（因变量）；$x_1, \dots, x_D$：**特征**（自变量）。

items.en: $\beta_0$: the **intercept** or bias, the prediction when all features are 0. $\beta_1, \dots, \beta_D$: the **weights**: $\beta_j$ is how much the prediction changes when $x_j$ grows by 1 and the other features stay fixed.
items.zh: $\beta_0$：**截距**（偏置），所有特征为 0 时的预测。$\beta_1, \dots, \beta_D$：**权重**：$\beta_j$ 是 $x_j$ 增加 1、其他特征不变时预测的变化量。

items.en: The trick $x_0 = 1$ folds the intercept into the dot product, so one formula $\boldsymbol\beta^\top\mathbf{x}$ covers everything. (The deck writes $\boldsymbol\beta$ where other lectures write $\boldsymbol\theta$.)
items.zh: 约定 $x_0 = 1$，把截距并进点积，一个式子 $\boldsymbol\beta^\top\mathbf{x}$ 就够了。（课件写 $\boldsymbol\beta$，别的讲座写 $\boldsymbol\theta$。）

text.en: The deck's other examples use several features at once: income from age, years of education and hours worked. Two assumptions come with the model: the relationship really is **linear** (a one-unit change in a feature always changes the prediction by the same amount), and the features are **not highly correlated with each other**, or the weights become unstable (see the closed-form page).
text.zh: 课件的另一些例子同时用多个特征：用年龄、受教育年数和工时预测收入。模型带着两条假设：关系确实是**线性**的（特征每变 1 个单位，预测总是变同样的量），以及特征之间**不能高度相关**，否则权重会不稳定（见闭式解那一页）。

body.en: Only predict inside the range of the training features (here 20 to 60 hours). Outside, nothing supports the line: the fitted line gives a **negative** income at 5 hours per week, and a straight line cannot keep going forever.
body.zh: 只在训练特征的范围内预测（这里是 20 到 60 小时）。范围之外没有数据支撑这条线：拟合出的线在每周 5 小时给出**负**收入，而直线不可能一直延伸下去。

prompt.en: A line fitted on hours worked between 20 and 60 is used to predict income at 100 hours per week. What is the problem?
prompt.zh: 用工时在 20 到 60 之间拟合的直线，去预测每周 100 小时的收入。问题在哪？

label.en: None: a line is defined for every $x$
label.zh: 没问题：直线对每个 $x$ 都有定义

feedback.en: Defined is not reliable: nothing in the data says the relationship stays linear out there (people at 100 hours may be burnt out, or paid by project).
feedback.zh: 有定义不等于可靠：数据里没有任何东西说明到那里关系还是线性的（100 小时的人也许已经透支，或者按项目拿钱）。

label.en: Extrapolation: the model is untested outside the data range, so the prediction is unreliable
label.zh: 外推：模型在数据范围之外没有验证过，预测不可靠

feedback.en: The intercept is the value at 0 hours, which is another extrapolation, not the reason this one fails.
feedback.zh: 截距是 0 小时的取值，那本身也是外推，并不是这里出问题的原因。

explain.en: Interpolation (inside the observed range) is safe; extrapolation is a guess.
explain.zh: 内插（在观测范围内）是安全的；外推只是猜测。

chapter.en: The loss and the closed form

title.zh: “最好的线”是什么意思：损失函数

alt.en: Ten income points, the least-squares line, and a vertical segment from each point to the line: the residual.
alt.zh: 十个收入点、最小二乘直线，以及每个点到直线的竖直线段：残差。

text.en: Many lines pass near the points. To pick **the** best one, measure each line's mistakes. The mistake on instance $i$ is the **residual** $\varepsilon_i = y_i - \hat y_i$, the vertical gap between the point and the line (the orange segments). Positive when the line is too low, negative when too high; if we just added them, the signs would cancel, so we square them first:
text.zh: 很多直线都从点附近经过。要选出**那一条**最好的，就得衡量每条线的错误。第 $i$ 个实例的错误是**残差** $\varepsilon_i = y_i - \hat y_i$，也就是点到直线的竖直距离（橙色线段）。线太低时为正，太高时为负；直接相加正负会抵消，所以先平方：

text.en: **Training** the model means finding the $\boldsymbol\beta$ that minimises this loss. Why squares? They are always positive, large mistakes count much more than small ones (twice as far off costs four times), and the function is smooth, so calculus works (next pages). The deck lists the alternatives: **RSS** (the sum), **MSE** (the mean), **RMSE** ($\sqrt{\text{MSE}}$, back in the units of $y$), **MAE** (mean of $|y_i - \hat y_i|$); only MSE is used for training in this lecture, and the others come with evaluation.
text.zh: **训练**模型就是找让这个损失最小的 $\boldsymbol\beta$。为什么平方？它总为正，大错误比小错误重得多（偏差两倍，代价四倍），而且函数光滑，可以用微积分（下几页）。课件列出的其他选择：**RSS**（和）、**MSE**（均值）、**RMSE**（$\sqrt{\text{MSE}}$，回到 $y$ 的单位）、**MAE**（$|y_i - \hat y_i|$ 的均值）；这一讲只用 MSE 来训练，其他的属于评估。

text.en: Picture the loss as a surface over the parameters $(\beta_0, \beta_1)$: for linear regression it is a smooth bowl with **one** lowest point (the deck draws it on slides 35-36). Training is finding the bottom of the bowl, which is what the next three pages do exactly (calculus) and, later, step by step (gradient descent).
text.zh: 把损失想成参数 $(\beta_0, \beta_1)$ 上方的一张曲面：对线性回归它是一个光滑的碗，只有**一个**最低点（课件第 35-36 页画了它）。训练就是找到碗底：接下来精确地做（微积分），再后面一步一步地做（梯度下降）。

title.en: Finding a minimum: set the derivative to zero

say.en: A warm-up with one parameter. At a minimum a smooth function is flat: its slope is zero. So the recipe is: write the function, differentiate, set the derivative to zero, solve.
say.zh: 一个参数的热身。光滑函数在最小值处是平的：斜率为零。所以步骤是：写出函数，求导，令导数为零，解出来。

say.en: The derivative is $2(\theta - 1)$; it is zero at $\theta = 1$. Because $f$ is a **convex** bowl, this flat point is the global minimum (for a concave function it would be the global maximum).
say.zh: 导数是 $2(\theta - 1)$，在 $\theta = 1$ 处为零。因为 $f$ 是**凸**的碗，这个平点就是全局最小（凹函数的话则是全局最大）。

say.en: The same recipe for the deck's spam model: $x$ spam among $N$ emails, likelihood $C\,\theta^{x}(1-\theta)^{N-x}$, $\theta = P(\text{spam})$. To maximise it, take the log first: the log is increasing, so the best $\theta$ is the same, and the product becomes a sum (easier derivatives, no underflow).
say.zh: 同样的步骤用在课件的垃圾邮件模型上：$N$ 封里有 $x$ 封垃圾，似然 $C\,\theta^{x}(1-\theta)^{N-x}$，$\theta = P(\text{spam})$。要最大化它，先取对数：对数递增，最优的 $\theta$ 不变，乘积变成和（导数更好求，也不会下溢）。

say.en: Differentiate: $\log C$ is a constant and disappears; $\log\theta$ gives $1/\theta$; $\log(1-\theta)$ gives $-1/(1-\theta)$ by the chain rule. Set it to zero.
say.zh: 求导：$\log C$ 是常数，消失；$\log\theta$ 的导数是 $1/\theta$；$\log(1-\theta)$ 由链式法则得 $-1/(1-\theta)$。令它为零。

say.en: Multiply through by $\theta(1-\theta)$ and expand: the $x\theta$ terms cancel.
say.zh: 两边乘以 $\theta(1-\theta)$ 并展开：$x\theta$ 项抵消。

say.en: The best $\theta$ is the observed fraction: 20 spam out of 100 emails gives 0.2. Same recipe, whatever the function.
say.zh: 最优的 $\theta$ 就是观察到的比例：100 封里 20 封垃圾邮件，得 0.2。不论函数是什么，步骤都一样。

intro.en: Training a model is optimisation: find the parameters that make an objective as small (a loss) or as large (a likelihood) as possible.
intro.zh: 训练模型就是优化：找参数，使目标函数尽可能小（损失）或尽可能大（似然）。

outro.en: Next, the same recipe with a vector $\boldsymbol\beta$ instead of a number $\theta$.
outro.zh: 接下来，同样的步骤，只是 $\theta$ 换成向量 $\boldsymbol\beta$。

title.en: Deeper: the normal equation by matrix calculus
title.zh: 深入：用矩阵微积分推出正规方程

say.en: Stack the data. $\mathbf{X}$ is the $n \times (D+1)$ matrix whose row $i$ is $\mathbf{x}_i^\top$ (first column all ones); $\mathbf{y}$ is the vector of the $n$ targets. Then $\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol\beta$ is the vector of all predictions at once, $\mathbf{y} - \mathbf{X}\boldsymbol\beta$ the vector of residuals, and a vector times its own transpose is the sum of its squared entries: this is $\frac1n\sum_i \varepsilon_i^2$.
say.zh: 把数据堆起来。$\mathbf{X}$ 是 $n \times (D+1)$ 的矩阵，第 $i$ 行是 $\mathbf{x}_i^\top$（第一列全是 1）；$\mathbf{y}$ 是 $n$ 个目标组成的向量。于是 $\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol\beta$ 是所有预测的向量，$\mathbf{y} - \mathbf{X}\boldsymbol\beta$ 是残差向量，向量乘自己的转置就是各分量平方和：这正是 $\frac1n\sum_i \varepsilon_i^2$。

say.en: Expand the product like $(a-b)^2$, remembering that $(\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol\beta)^\top = \boldsymbol\beta^\top\mathbf{X}^\top$ (a transpose reverses the order).
say.zh: 像 $(a-b)^2$ 一样展开，注意 $(\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol\beta)^\top = \boldsymbol\beta^\top\mathbf{X}^\top$（转置会把顺序反过来）。

say.en: The two middle terms are the same number: each is a $1 \times 1$ matrix (a scalar), and a scalar equals its own transpose. Combine them. This is the form on the deck's slide 37.
say.zh: 中间两项是同一个数：它们都是 $1 \times 1$ 矩阵（标量），而标量等于它自己的转置。合并。这就是课件第 37 页的形式。

say.en: Two rules of matrix calculus (gradient = the vector of partial derivatives). First: $\mathbf{a}^\top\boldsymbol\beta = \sum_j a_j\beta_j$, whose derivative with respect to $\beta_j$ is $a_j$. Second, for a **symmetric** matrix $\mathbf{A}$: the quadratic form $\boldsymbol\beta^\top\mathbf{A}\boldsymbol\beta$ is the multi-dimensional version of $a\beta^2$, whose derivative is $2a\beta$.
say.zh: 两条矩阵微积分规则（梯度 = 偏导数组成的向量）。第一条：$\mathbf{a}^\top\boldsymbol\beta = \sum_j a_j\beta_j$，对 $\beta_j$ 的导数是 $a_j$。第二条，$\mathbf{A}$ 为**对称**矩阵时：二次型 $\boldsymbol\beta^\top\mathbf{A}\boldsymbol\beta$ 是 $a\beta^2$ 的多维版本，导数是 $2a\beta$。

why.en: $\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ is symmetric: $(\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X})^\top = \mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$. It plays the role of $\mathbf{A}$, and $\mathbf{a}^\top = \mathbf{y}^\top\mathbf{X}$, i.e. $\mathbf{a} = \mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{y}$.

say.en: Differentiate term by term: $\mathbf{y}^\top\mathbf{y}$ has no $\boldsymbol\beta$, so its derivative is 0; the other two use the rules. This is slide 38.
say.zh: 逐项求导：$\mathbf{y}^\top\mathbf{y}$ 里没有 $\boldsymbol\beta$，导数为 0；另两项用上面两条规则。这是课件第 38 页。

say.en: Set the gradient to zero and drop the factor $2/n$. This is the **normal equation**: $D+1$ linear equations in the $D+1$ unknown weights.
say.zh: 令梯度为零，去掉因子 $2/n$。这就是**正规方程**：$D+1$ 个未知权重的 $D+1$ 个线性方程。

say.en: Multiply both sides by the inverse of $\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$, if it exists. This is the closed form: no iterations, one formula.
say.zh: 两边左乘 $\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ 的逆（如果存在）。这就是闭式解：不用迭代，一个公式。

say.en: Is the flat point a minimum, not a maximum or saddle? The second derivative (the Hessian) is $\frac2n\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$. For any vector $\mathbf{v}$, $\mathbf{v}^\top\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}\mathbf{v} = \lVert\mathbf{X}\mathbf{v}\rVert^2 \ge 0$, so the Hessian is positive semi-definite: MSE is **convex**, a bowl, and any point with zero gradient is a global minimum.
say.zh: 这个平点是最小值，而不是最大值或鞍点吗？二阶导数（海森矩阵）是 $\frac2n\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$。对任意向量 $\mathbf{v}$，$\mathbf{v}^\top\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}\mathbf{v} = \lVert\mathbf{X}\mathbf{v}\rVert^2 \ge 0$，所以海森矩阵半正定：MSE 是**凸**的（一个碗），梯度为零的点都是全局最小。

intro.en: The deck states this result and says its derivation is not examined (slides 37-38: \"the specific formulas will not be part of any assignment or exam\"). Doing it once makes the formula something you can rebuild, not memorise.
intro.zh: 课件给出了这个结果，并说明推导不考（第 37-38 页：具体公式不会出现在作业或考试里）。亲手做一遍，公式就是可以重建的，而不是死记的。

outro.en: The one thing worth remembering for the exam is the shape of the result: $\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol\beta = \mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{y}$, and that it needs $\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ to be invertible.
outro.zh: 考试里值得记的是结果的形状：$\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol\beta = \mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{y}$，以及它要求 $\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ 可逆。

title.en: The deck's income data, by hand

say.en: With one feature the normal equation has a simple solution. First the two means. The best line always passes through the point $(\bar x, \bar y)$.
say.zh: 只有一个特征时，正规方程有简单的解。先算两个均值。最优直线一定经过点 $(\bar x, \bar y)$。

say.en: $S_{xy}$ measures how $x$ and $y$ move together (positive here: more hours, more income); $S_{xx}$ measures how much $x$ varies.
say.zh: $S_{xy}$ 衡量 $x$ 和 $y$ 怎么一起变（这里为正：工时多、收入高）；$S_{xx}$ 衡量 $x$ 自己的波动。

say.en: The slope is the covariance over the variance: each extra weekly hour is associated with about $1.48$K more income.
say.zh: 斜率是协方差除以方差：每周多工作一小时，对应收入约多 $1.48$ 千美元。

say.en: The line goes through $(\bar x, \bar y)$, so the intercept follows from the slope.
say.zh: 直线经过 $(\bar x, \bar y)$，所以截距可由斜率推出。

say.en: The fitted line. Hand-check the matrix formula? For one feature, $(\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{y}$ gives exactly these two numbers.
say.zh: 拟合出的直线。用矩阵公式核对？一个特征时，$(\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{y}$ 给出的正是这两个数。

say.en: A prediction inside the data range (20 to 60 hours): about 31.5K for 30 hours per week.
say.zh: 数据范围（20 到 60 小时）内的一个预测：每周 30 小时约 31.5 千美元。

outro.en: A detail: slides 36 and 39 quote $-13.13 + 1.48x$, the lowest point found on a grid of $(\beta_0, \beta_1)$ values. The exact least-squares line is $-12.79 + 1.477\,x$; its MSE is 119.79, the grid point's 119.85. If an exam gives you a line, use the numbers given; if it asks you to fit, use the formulas.
outro.zh: 一个细节：课件第 36 和 39 页给的是 $-13.13 + 1.48x$，那是在 $(\beta_0, \beta_1)$ 网格上找到的最低点。精确的最小二乘直线是 $-12.79 + 1.477\,x$，MSE 为 119.79，网格点的是 119.85。考试给你一条线就用给定的数；要你拟合就用公式。

title.zh: 闭式解什么时候出问题

text.en: $\hat{\boldsymbol\beta} = (\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{y}$ needs $\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ to be invertible. It is not when one feature is an exact linear combination of the others (an hours column duplicated, or \"age in years\" and \"age in months\"): then infinitely many $\boldsymbol\beta$ give the same predictions and the normal equation has no unique solution. When features are **highly correlated** but not identical, the inverse exists but is numerically unstable: tiny changes in the data swing the weights wildly, and individual weights lose their meaning (the deck: \"the inverse matrix becomes unstable\"). This is **multicollinearity**.
text.zh: $\hat{\boldsymbol\beta} = (\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{y}$ 要求 $\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ 可逆。当某个特征是其他特征的精确线性组合时（工时那一列重复了一份，或同时放“年龄（岁）”和“年龄（月）”）它不可逆：有无穷多个 $\boldsymbol\beta$ 给出同样的预测，正规方程没有唯一解。特征**高度相关**但不完全相同时，逆存在，但数值上不稳定：数据的微小变化会让权重大幅摆动，单个权重失去意义（课件：逆矩阵变得不稳定）。这就是**多重共线性**。

items.en: **Remedies:** drop or combine redundant features; collect more varied data; or **regularise** (below).
items.zh: **对策：**删除或合并冗余特征；收集更多样的数据；或**正则化**（见下）。

items.en: The weights are also not comparable across features when the features have different units; scaling makes them comparable (and is essential for gradient descent).
items.zh: 特征单位不同时，权重之间没法比较；缩放后才可比（对梯度下降尤其必要）。

summary.en: Beyond the deck: ridge and lasso regularisation
summary.zh: 课件之外：岭回归与 lasso 正则化

text.en: **Ridge** adds a penalty on the size of the weights: minimise $\text{MSE} + \lambda\lVert\boldsymbol\beta\rVert^2$ (not penalising $\beta_0$). The solution is $(\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X} + n\lambda\mathbf{I})^{-1}\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{y}$: adding a positive amount to the diagonal makes the matrix always invertible and stabilises correlated features. **Lasso** penalises $\sum_j|\beta_j|$ instead and drives some weights exactly to zero, which selects features (see the feature-selection lesson). $\lambda$ trades bias for variance, like $\alpha$ in smoothing.
text.zh: **岭回归**对权重大小加惩罚：最小化 $\text{MSE} + \lambda\lVert\boldsymbol\beta\rVert^2$（不惩罚 $\beta_0$）。解为 $(\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X} + n\lambda\mathbf{I})^{-1}\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{y}$：对角线加一个正数，矩阵就一定可逆，相关特征也稳定下来。**Lasso** 改为惩罚 $\sum_j|\beta_j|$，会把一些权重压到恰好为零，从而选出特征（见特征选择一课）。$\lambda$ 用偏差换方差，类似平滑里的 $\alpha$。

text.en: Standard sources: Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman, *The Elements of Statistical Learning*, ch. 3; Bishop, *PRML*, §3.1.4. This is beyond what lecture 7 covers.
text.zh: 标准参考：Hastie、Tibshirani、Friedman《统计学习基础》第 3 章；Bishop《模式识别与机器学习》§3.1.4。这超出了第 7 讲的内容。

title.en: Deeper: least squares is maximum likelihood under Gaussian noise
title.zh: 深入：最小二乘就是高斯噪声下的最大似然

say.en: A probabilistic story for the line: the target is the linear prediction plus noise. The noise is a bell curve with mean 0 and the same variance $\sigma^2$ for every instance, and independent between instances.
say.zh: 给这条线配一个概率故事：目标 = 线性预测 + 噪声。噪声是均值为 0、方差对所有实例都是 $\sigma^2$ 的钟形曲线，且实例之间相互独立。

say.en: So $y_i$ is Gaussian with mean $\boldsymbol\beta^\top\mathbf{x}_i$ and variance $\sigma^2$. This is the Gaussian density of Lecture 4, evaluated at the actual target.
say.zh: 所以 $y_i$ 服从均值 $\boldsymbol\beta^\top\mathbf{x}_i$、方差 $\sigma^2$ 的高斯分布。这就是第 4 讲的高斯密度，在真实目标处取值。

say.en: The likelihood of the whole data set: because the instances are independent, multiply the densities.
say.zh: 整个数据集的似然：实例独立，所以把各密度相乘。

say.en: Take the log (product to sum, and $\log e^{u} = u$ removes the exponential).
say.zh: 取对数（乘积变和，$\log e^{u} = u$ 去掉指数）。

say.en: Pull out the constants. The last sum is exactly the RSS.
say.zh: 提出常数。最后那个和正是 RSS。

say.en: As far as $\boldsymbol\beta$ is concerned, the first term is a constant, and the second is minus a positive number times the RSS. Maximising the likelihood is minimising the sum of squared errors: **the least-squares line is the maximum likelihood line** (dividing by $n$ changes nothing).
say.zh: 就 $\boldsymbol\beta$ 而言，第一项是常数，第二项是“负的正数乘以 RSS”。最大化似然就是最小化误差平方和：**最小二乘直线就是最大似然直线**（除以 $n$ 不影响）。

say.en: A bonus: set the derivative with respect to the noise variance to zero. The estimated noise variance is the MSE of the best line, so the MSE is also the estimate of how noisy the data are.
say.zh: 附送一个结果：对噪声方差求导并令其为零。估计出的噪声方差就是最优直线的 MSE，所以 MSE 同时也是对“数据有多嘈杂”的估计。

intro.en: Why squared error and not, say, absolute error? One answer: a modelling assumption about the noise.
intro.zh: 为什么是平方误差，而不是绝对误差之类？一个回答：它对应一个关于噪声的建模假设。

chapter.en: Why least squares: the maximum likelihood view
chapter.zh: 为什么用最小二乘：最大似然的视角

title.en: Deeper: what the maximum likelihood view tells you
title.zh: 深入：最大似然视角告诉了你什么

items.en: **Squared error silently assumes Gaussian noise with constant variance.** Where that is wrong, least squares is not the natural choice.
items.zh: **平方误差悄悄假设了方差恒定的高斯噪声。**这个假设不对时，最小二乘就不是自然的选择。

items.en: **Outliers hurt.** A Gaussian has thin tails: a point far from the line is astronomically unlikely, so the fit bends towards it to make it less unlikely. In loss terms, a point 10 units off costs 100, ten points 1 unit off cost only 10. (The deck lists this as a weakness.) Assuming heavier-tailed **Laplace** noise gives absolute error (MAE), which is more robust.
items.zh: **离群点伤害大。**高斯的尾巴很细：离直线很远的点几乎不可能出现，拟合于是向它弯过去，让它“没那么不可能”。用损失的话说：偏差 10 的点代价 100，十个偏差 1 的点才共 10。（课件把它列为缺点。）若假设尾巴更厚的**拉普拉斯**噪声，得到的就是绝对误差（MAE），更稳健。

items.en: **Regularisation is a prior.** A Gaussian prior on the weights turns the maximum likelihood estimate into the MAP estimate, which is ridge regression: the same bridge as Laplace smoothing in the naive Bayes lesson.
items.zh: **正则化就是先验。**给权重加高斯先验，最大似然估计就变成 MAP 估计，也就是岭回归：和朴素贝叶斯那一课里拉普拉斯平滑是同一座桥。

prompt.en: A data set has a few extreme outliers. Which change reduces their influence on the fitted line?
prompt.zh: 数据集里有几个极端离群点。哪种改变能减小它们对拟合直线的影响？

label.en: Use MSE with a smaller learning rate

feedback.en: The learning rate changes how fast we descend, not where the minimum is; the outliers still dominate the loss.
feedback.zh: 学习率只影响下降的快慢，不影响最小值的位置；离群点仍然主导损失。

label.en: Use absolute error (MAE) instead of squared error
label.zh: 改用绝对误差（MAE）代替平方误差

feedback.en: More features give the model more freedom to chase the outliers; they do not reduce their weight in the loss.
feedback.zh: 更多特征让模型更自由地去迁就离群点，并不会减小它们在损失里的权重。

explain.en: Squared error penalises large residuals quadratically; absolute error only linearly.
explain.zh: 平方误差对大残差按平方惩罚；绝对误差只按线性惩罚。

title.zh: 沿着坡往下走：梯度下降

text.en: The closed form is neat but uses a special fact (MSE has a solvable gradient equation). Most models, logistic regression and neural networks included, have no such formula. Gradient descent needs only the gradient: stand somewhere on the loss surface, feel which way is steepest **uphill** (the gradient $\nabla L$), and step the other way. Repeat.
text.zh: 闭式解很漂亮，但它用了一个特殊事实（MSE 的梯度方程可以解出来）。大多数模型，包括逻辑回归和神经网络，都没有这样的公式。梯度下降只需要梯度：站在损失曲面上的某处，感觉哪个方向**上坡**最陡（梯度 $\nabla L$），朝相反方向迈一步，重复。

items.en: The gradient points uphill, so the **minus** sign makes us go downhill. At the minimum the gradient is 0 and the updates stop.
items.zh: 梯度指向上坡，所以**减号**让我们往下走。到了最小值，梯度为 0，更新自然停下。

items.en: $\eta > 0$ is the **learning rate**, the step size. It is a setting you choose, not learned from the data.
items.zh: $\eta > 0$ 是**学习率**，即步长。它是你选的设置，不是从数据里学到的。

items.en: Because MSE is convex there is **one** valley: gradient descent cannot get stuck in a local minimum, whatever the start.
items.zh: MSE 是凸的，只有**一个**谷：不论从哪出发，梯度下降都不会困在局部最小。

text.en: This lecture sets up the idea (Lecture 8 develops iterative optimisation). What the learning rate does is easy to see on $f(\theta) = (\theta-1)^2$, whose update is $\theta \leftarrow \theta - 2\eta(\theta - 1)$, i.e. the distance to the minimum is multiplied by $1 - 2\eta$ each step. Starting at $\theta = 3$:
text.zh: 这一讲只引入想法（第 8 讲会展开迭代优化）。学习率的作用在 $f(\theta) = (\theta-1)^2$ 上很容易看清：更新是 $\theta \leftarrow \theta - 2\eta(\theta - 1)$，即每步到最小值的距离乘以 $1 - 2\eta$。从 $\theta = 3$ 出发：

text.en: $\eta = 0.1$: a steady crawl towards 1 (factor 0.8 per step). $\eta = 0.9$: overshoots to the other side each time but shrinks (factor $-0.8$). $\eta = 1.1$: factor $-1.2$, so each step lands **farther** away: divergence. Too small is slow, too large explodes; the loss should fall at each step, and if it rises, lower $\eta$.
text.zh: $\eta = 0.1$：稳稳地往 1 爬（每步因子 0.8）。$\eta = 0.9$：每次都冲到另一侧，但在缩小（因子 $-0.8$）。$\eta = 1.1$：因子 $-1.2$，每一步都落得**更远**：发散。太小则慢，太大则爆；损失应该每步下降，如果上升就调小 $\eta$。

body.en: If one feature is in the thousands and another between 0 and 1, the loss bowl is a long narrow valley: a step size that is safe along the steep direction crawls along the flat one. Standardising each feature, $x \leftarrow (x - \text{mean})/\text{std}$, makes the bowl round, so one $\eta$ suits all weights. The closed form does not need scaling (the weights simply rescale).
body.zh: 如果一个特征在千的量级，另一个在 0 到 1 之间，损失的碗就是一道又长又窄的谷：在陡的方向上安全的步长，在平的方向上就慢得像爬。把每个特征标准化，$x \leftarrow (x - \text{均值})/\text{标准差}$，碗就变圆了，一个 $\eta$ 对所有权重都合适。闭式解不需要缩放（权重只是相应缩放）。

title.en: The gradient of MSE, one weight at a time
title.zh: MSE 的梯度，一个权重一个权重地求

say.en: One feature, so two weights. $\hat y_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_i$ inside the square.
say.zh: 一个特征，两个权重。平方里是 $\hat y_i = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x_i$。

say.en: Chain rule: the derivative of $u^2$ is $2u$, times the derivative of the inside $u = y_i - \beta_0 - \beta_1 x_i$ with respect to $\beta_0$, which is $-1$.
say.zh: 链式法则：$u^2$ 的导数是 $2u$，乘以内部 $u = y_i - \beta_0 - \beta_1 x_i$ 对 $\beta_0$ 的导数，即 $-1$。

say.en: Tidy: minus twice the average residual. If the line is on average too low (positive residuals), the gradient is negative and the update $-\eta\cdot$gradient **raises** $\beta_0$.
say.zh: 整理：负的两倍平均残差。线平均偏低（残差为正）时，梯度为负，更新 $-\eta\cdot$梯度就会**抬高** $\beta_0$。

say.en: For $\beta_1$ the inside's derivative is $-x_i$, so each residual is weighted by its feature value: the slope is corrected most by the instances with large $x_i$.
say.zh: 对 $\beta_1$，内部的导数是 $-x_i$，所以每个残差按其特征值加权：斜率主要由 $x_i$ 大的实例来修正。

say.en: The update rule, with $\varepsilon_i = y_i - \hat y_i$: move each weight in the direction that reduces the residuals. For many features, $\beta_j \leftarrow \beta_j + \frac{2\eta}{n}\sum_i \varepsilon_i x_{ij}$, which is the matrix form $\frac{2}{n}\mathbf{X}^\top(\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol\beta - \mathbf{y})$ of the previous page.
say.zh: 更新规则，$\varepsilon_i = y_i - \hat y_i$：把每个权重朝能减小残差的方向移动。特征很多时，$\beta_j \leftarrow \beta_j + \frac{2\eta}{n}\sum_i \varepsilon_i x_{ij}$，也就是上一页的矩阵形式 $\frac{2}{n}\mathbf{X}^\top(\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol\beta - \mathbf{y})$。

title.en: Two steps of gradient descent by hand

say.en: A tiny data set, start at $\beta_0 = \beta_1 = 0$ (predict 0 everywhere), $\eta = 0.05$. All residuals are just the targets: $2, 3, 5, 6$.
say.zh: 一个很小的数据集，从 $\beta_0 = \beta_1 = 0$ 出发（处处预测 0），$\eta = 0.05$。所有残差就是目标本身：$2, 3, 5, 6$。

say.en: Gradient for $\beta_0$: minus twice the mean residual.
say.zh: $\beta_0$ 的梯度：负的两倍平均残差。

say.en: Gradient for $\beta_1$: residuals weighted by $x$: $2 + 6 + 15 + 24 = 47$, times $-\frac24$.
Update: both gradients are negative (the line is too low), so both weights increase.
say.zh: 更新：两个梯度都是负的（线太低），所以两个权重都增加。

say.en: The slope update. After one step the line is $0.40 + 1.175\,x$.
say.zh: 斜率的更新。一步之后直线是 $0.40 + 1.175\,x$。

say.en: Repeat with the new residuals. The gradients are far smaller (the line is already close), so the steps shrink: gradient descent slows down as it nears the bottom.
say.zh: 用新的残差重复。梯度小得多（线已经很接近了），所以步子变小：梯度下降在接近谷底时自然放慢。

outro.en: After 300 steps the weights are $(0.500,\ 1.400)$; the closed form gives $(0.500,\ 1.400)$: the same line, reached by two routes.

prompt.en: What is $\beta_1$ after one step? Compute $0 - 0.05 \cdot (-23.5)$.
prompt.zh: 一步之后 $\beta_1$ 是多少？算 $0 - 0.05 \cdot (-23.5)$。

rows.en: the exact minimum in one shot
rows.zh: 一步到位的精确最小值

rows.en: approaches the minimum; stop when the loss stops falling
rows.zh: 逐步逼近最小值；损失不再下降时停

rows.en: $O(nD)$ per step, times the number of steps
few features (up to thousands), data fits in memory
rows.zh: 特征不多（至多几千），数据能放进内存

rows.en: many features or huge $n$ (use a random mini-batch per step: stochastic gradient descent)
rows.zh: 特征很多或 $n$ 极大（每步用随机小批量：随机梯度下降）

rows.en: learning rate $\eta$, number of steps; scale the features
rows.zh: 学习率 $\eta$、步数；要缩放特征

rows.en: slow if badly scaled; diverges if $\eta$ is too big
rows.zh: 缩放不好时很慢；$\eta$ 太大会发散
只适用于线性最小二乘

rows.en: works for any differentiable loss (logistic regression, neural networks)
rows.zh: 适用于任何可微损失（逻辑回归、神经网络）

text.en: In practice software rarely forms $(\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X})^{-1}$ explicitly: it solves the equations with a numerically stable factorisation (QR or SVD). The formula is for understanding; the factorisation is for computing. Both approaches find the same line because the loss has only one valley.
text.zh: 实际中软件很少真的去算 $(\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X})^{-1}$，而是用数值稳定的分解（QR 或 SVD）来解方程。公式用于理解，分解用于计算。两种办法找到同一条线，因为这个损失只有一个谷。

prompt.en: During gradient descent the training loss goes up at every step. What do you try first?
prompt.zh: 梯度下降时训练损失每步都在上升。你先试什么？

label.en: A larger learning rate, to move faster
label.zh: 更大的学习率，走得快一点

feedback.en: A rising loss means the steps overshoot the valley; a larger step overshoots more.
feedback.zh: 损失上升说明步子冲过了谷；步子更大冲得更远。

feedback.en: That works for this model but does not answer the question; with a non-linear model there is no closed form to switch to.
feedback.zh: 对这个模型可行，但没回答问题；换成非线性模型就没有闭式解可换了。

label.en: A smaller learning rate (and check the feature scales)
label.zh: 更小的学习率（并检查特征尺度）

explain.en: Divergence means $\eta$ is too large for the loss surface; lower it, or standardise features.
explain.zh: 发散说明 $\eta$ 对这个损失曲面来说太大；调小它，或标准化特征。

title.en: How good is the line? RSS, MSE, RMSE, MAE, R²

text.en: The same residuals give several summaries. On the income data with the fitted line:
text.zh: 同一组残差可以给出几种概括。对收入数据和拟合的直线：

rows.zh: 总平方误差；随 $n$ 增长

rows.en: average squared error; units of $y$ squared
rows.zh: 平均平方误差；单位是 $y$ 的平方

rows.en: typical error in the units of $y$: about 10.9 thousand dollars here
rows.zh: 以 $y$ 为单位的典型误差：这里约 10.9 千美元

rows.en: average absolute error; less dominated by outliers
rows.zh: 平均绝对误差；受离群点影响较小

rows.en: share of the variance of $y$ explained by the line
rows.zh: 直线解释掉的 $y$ 的方差占比

text.en: $\text{TSS} = \sum_i (y_i - \bar y)^2 = 4057.6$ is the error of the dumbest model, always predicting the mean $\bar y$. So $R^2 = 1$ means a perfect fit, $R^2 = 0$ no better than the mean (it can go negative on new data for a model worse than the mean). Here the hours explain about 70% of the variation in income.
text.zh: $\text{TSS} = \sum_i (y_i - \bar y)^2 = 4057.6$ 是最笨的模型（永远预测均值 $\bar y$）的误差。所以 $R^2 = 1$ 是完美拟合，$R^2 = 0$ 不比均值好（在新数据上，比均值还差的模型 $R^2$ 可以为负）。这里工时解释了收入变化的约 70%。

title.en: Measure on data the model has not seen
title.zh: 要在模型没见过的数据上衡量

body.en: Training $R^2$ never falls when you add features, even useless ones: a model can chase noise. Judge a regression on held-out data (the evaluation lesson), where the choice of metric and the train/test split matter.
body.zh: 加特征时训练集上的 $R^2$ 永远不会下降，哪怕特征毫无用处：模型可以在追噪声。回归模型要在留出数据上评判（评估一课），那里指标的选择和训练/测试划分才是关键。

rows.en: each weight is the effect of a feature, others fixed
rows.zh: 每个权重是其他特征不变时该特征的作用

rows.en: normal equations: no iterative training for small data
rows.zh: 正规方程：数据小时不用迭代训练

rows.en: curved relationships are missed unless you add transformed features
rows.zh: 弯曲的关系抓不住，除非加变换后的特征

rows.en: correlated features make $\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ unstable and weights unreliable
rows.zh: 相关特征让 $\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ 不稳定、权重不可靠

rows.en: squared error: one far point can tilt the line (Gaussian-noise assumption)
rows.zh: 平方误差：一个远点就能把线拉歪（高斯噪声假设）

rows.en: the line has no support outside the data range
rows.zh: 数据范围之外这条线没有依据

rows.en: Normal equations costly for many features
rows.zh: 特征很多时正规方程代价大

prompt.en: Using the exact least-squares line of the income data, $\hat y = -12.786 + 1.4774\,x$, what is the predicted income (in thousands of dollars) for 50 hours per week? One decimal.
prompt.zh: 用收入数据的精确最小二乘直线 $\hat y = -12.786 + 1.4774\,x$，每周 50 小时的预测收入是多少（千美元）？保留一位小数。

explain.en: $-12.786 + 1.4774 \times 50 = 61.1$. It is inside the data range (20 to 60), so interpolation.

prompt.en: Fit $\hat y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x$ to $(1, 3), (2, 5), (3, 4)$ by gradient descent on the MSE, starting at $\beta_0 = \beta_1 = 0$ with $\eta = 0.1$. What is $\beta_1$ after **one** step? Three decimals.
prompt.zh: 用 MSE 的梯度下降，对 $(1, 3), (2, 5), (3, 4)$ 拟合 $\hat y = \beta_0 + \beta_1 x$，从 $\beta_0 = \beta_1 = 0$ 出发，$\eta = 0.1$。**一步**之后 $\beta_1$ 是多少？保留三位小数。

explain.en: Residuals at the start are the targets $3, 5, 4$. $g_1 = -\frac{2}{3}(3\cdot1 + 5\cdot2 + 4\cdot3) = -16.6667$. So $\beta_1 = 0 - 0.1 \cdot g_1 = 1.667$ (and $\beta_0 = 0.800$).

prompt.en: A model predicts $\hat y = 3, 4, 6$ for the true values $y = 2, 4, 9$. What is the MSE? Three decimals.
prompt.zh: 模型对真实值 $y = 2, 4, 9$ 预测 $\hat y = 3, 4, 6$。MSE 是多少？保留三位小数。

explain.en: Residuals $-1, 0, 3$; squares $1, 0, 9$; mean $\frac{10}{3} = 3.333$. (RMSE $= 1.826$.) Note the one big miss supplies 90% of the loss.

title.zh: 检查：两个一模一样的特征

prompt.en: You add a copy of an existing feature to $\mathbf{X}$ and use the normal equation. What happens?
prompt.zh: 你把一个已有的特征复制一列加进 $\mathbf{X}$，再用正规方程。会怎样？

label.en: The fit improves because the feature now counts twice
label.zh: 拟合变好，因为这个特征现在算了两次

feedback.en: The model can only combine the two columns as $(\beta_a + \beta_b)x$: no new information, no better fit.
feedback.zh: 模型只能把两列合并为 $(\beta_a + \beta_b)x$：没有新信息，也不会更好。

label.en: $\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ is singular, so there is no unique solution
Nothing: the weights are just halved

feedback.en: Splitting the weight in half is one of infinitely many equally good solutions, which is exactly why the solution is not unique and the inverse does not exist.
feedback.zh: 权重各减半只是无穷多个同样好的解之一，这正说明解不唯一、逆不存在。

explain.en: Identical columns make $\mathbf{X}$ rank deficient, so $\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ cannot be inverted; near-identical columns give an unstable inverse.
explain.zh: 两列相同使 $\mathbf{X}$ 秩亏，$\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}$ 无法求逆；近乎相同则逆不稳定。

prompt.en: Minimising the sum of squared errors is exactly maximum likelihood when we assume that the noise is:
prompt.zh: 最小化误差平方和，恰好等价于最大似然，当我们假设噪声是：

label.en: Gaussian with constant variance, independent between instances
label.zh: 方差恒定的高斯噪声，实例之间独立

feedback.en: That gives the sum of **absolute** errors (MAE).
feedback.zh: 那得到的是**绝对**误差之和（MAE）。

feedback.en: A uniform noise gives a flat likelihood inside the range and zero outside: no squared error appears.
feedback.zh: 均匀噪声在范围内似然是平的、范围外为零：不会出现平方误差。

explain.en: Log-likelihood of Gaussian noise contains $-(y - \boldsymbol\beta^\top\mathbf{x})^2/(2\sigma^2)$: maximising it is minimising squares.
explain.zh: 高斯噪声的对数似然里含 $-(y - \boldsymbol\beta^\top\mathbf{x})^2/(2\sigma^2)$：最大化它就是最小化平方和。

prompt.en: On $f(\theta) = (\theta - 1)^2$ gradient descent multiplies the distance to the minimum by $1 - 2\eta$ each step. For which $\eta$ does it **diverge**?
prompt.zh: 对 $f(\theta) = (\theta - 1)^2$，梯度下降每步把到最小值的距离乘以 $1 - 2\eta$。$\eta$ 取哪个会**发散**？

feedback.en: $|1 - 1.8| = 0.8 < 1$: it overshoots from side to side but the distance shrinks, so it still converges.
feedback.zh: $|1 - 1.8| = 0.8 < 1$：来回冲过头，但距离在缩小，所以仍然收敛。

feedback.en: Factor $0.98$: very slow but converging. Too small is inefficient, not divergent.
feedback.zh: 因子 $0.98$：很慢但收敛。太小是低效，不是发散。

title.en: Short answer: closed form vs gradient descent
title.zh: 简答：闭式解与梯度下降

prompt.en: Compare the normal equation and gradient descent for fitting a linear regression: what does each need, and when would you prefer each? (2-3 lines)
prompt.zh: 比较用正规方程和梯度下降拟合线性回归：各需要什么，什么时候选哪个？（2-3 行）

key_points.en: Normal equation: exact solution in one step, needs X^T X invertible, cost cubic in the number of features
key_points.zh: Normal equation: exact solution in one step, needs X^T X invertible, cost cubic in the number of features

key_points.en: Gradient descent: iterative, needs a learning rate and feature scaling, cheap per step, scales to many features or data
key_points.zh: Gradient descent: iterative, needs a learning rate and feature scaling, cheap per step, scales to many features or data

key_points.en: Prefer the closed form for few features; gradient descent for many features/large data or models without a closed form
key_points.zh: Prefer the closed form for few features; gradient descent for many features/large data or models without a closed form

model_answer.en: The normal equation gives the exact minimiser of the MSE in one step, beta = (X^T X)^{-1} X^T y, but it needs X^T X to be invertible (no collinear features) and costs about cubic time in the number of features. Gradient descent repeatedly moves beta against the gradient with a learning rate eta; each step is cheap, it needs a good eta and scaled features, but it scales to many features and large data and works for models with no closed form. Use the normal equation for small problems and gradient descent for large ones; both reach the same line because MSE is convex.
model_answer.zh: The normal equation gives the exact minimiser of the MSE in one step, beta = (X^T X)^{-1} X^T y, but it needs X^T X to be invertible (no collinear features) and costs about cubic time in the number of features. Gradient descent repeatedly moves beta against the gradient with a learning rate eta; each step is cheap, it needs a good eta and scaled features, but it scales to many features and large data and works for models with no closed form. Use the normal equation for small problems and gradient descent for large ones; both reach the same line because MSE is convex.

explain.en: Cover cost, invertibility, learning rate and when to use which.
explain.zh: 要点：代价、可逆性、学习率，以及何时用哪个。

prompt.en: You want to predict house prices from 200 features (floor area, rooms, a few hundred neighbourhood measures, many of them strongly correlated). A few sales are mansions at ten times the typical price. Describe how you would use linear regression: the model and loss, how you fit it, what problems you expect from the data, and how you would evaluate the result.
prompt.zh: 要用 200 个特征（面积、房间数、几百项社区指标，其中很多彼此强相关）预测房价；有几笔豪宅成交价是普通房的十倍。说明你会怎样用线性回归：模型和损失、怎么拟合、预计数据会带来什么问题、怎样评估结果。

key_points.en: Model price = beta^T x with MSE loss, fit by the normal equation or gradient descent (scaled features)
key_points.zh: Model price = beta^T x with MSE loss, fit by the normal equation or gradient descent (scaled features)

key_points.en: Correlated features: multicollinearity makes weights unstable; drop/combine features or use regularisation (ridge/lasso)
key_points.zh: Correlated features: multicollinearity makes weights unstable; drop/combine features or use regularisation (ridge/lasso)

key_points.en: Outliers: squared error is sensitive; consider robust loss (MAE) or transforming the target (log price)
key_points.zh: Outliers: squared error is sensitive; consider robust loss (MAE) or transforming the target (log price)

key_points.en: Evaluate on held-out data with RMSE/MAE and R^2; do not extrapolate beyond the data range
key_points.zh: Evaluate on held-out data with RMSE/MAE and R^2; do not extrapolate beyond the data range

model_answer.en: Model: price = beta_0 + sum_j beta_j x_j, trained by minimising the MSE, either with the normal equation or, with 200 features and many houses, gradient descent on standardised features. The strongly correlated neighbourhood features cause multicollinearity: X^T X is unstable and individual weights are unreliable, so I would drop or combine redundant features or add ridge or lasso regularisation. The mansions are outliers that squared error weights heavily; I would check their influence, consider a more robust loss such as MAE, or model log price. I would evaluate on a held-out test set with RMSE or MAE (in dollars) and R^2, and avoid predicting for houses far outside the training range.
model_answer.zh: Model: price = beta_0 + sum_j beta_j x_j, trained by minimising the MSE, either with the normal equation or, with 200 features and many houses, gradient descent on standardised features. The strongly correlated neighbourhood features cause multicollinearity: X^T X is unstable and individual weights are unreliable, so I would drop or combine redundant features or add ridge or lasso regularisation. The mansions are outliers that squared error weights heavily; I would check their influence, consider a more robust loss such as MAE, or model log price. I would evaluate on a held-out test set with RMSE or MAE (in dollars) and R^2, and avoid predicting for houses far outside the training range.

explain.en: Mention the model, fitting method, collinearity, outliers and held-out evaluation.
explain.zh: 要点：模型、拟合方法、共线性、离群点和留出集评估。

items.en: **Model:** weighted sum of features plus intercept (use $x_0 = 1$). Interpolate; do not extrapolate.
items.zh: **模型：**特征的加权和加截距（取 $x_0 = 1$）。可以内插，不要外推。

items.en: **Loss:** squared residuals (RSS, MSE; RMSE in the units of $y$; MAE less outlier-sensitive). Convex: one minimum.
items.zh: **损失：**残差平方（RSS、MSE；RMSE 的单位与 $y$ 相同；MAE 对离群点不那么敏感）。凸：只有一个最小值。

items.en: **Closed form:** $\hat{\boldsymbol\beta} = (\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{y}$, from setting the gradient $\frac2n(\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol\beta - \mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{y})$ to zero. Fails or is unstable with collinear features; costly ($O(D^3)$) for many features.
items.zh: **闭式解：**$\hat{\boldsymbol\beta} = (\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{y}$，由令梯度 $\frac2n(\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X}\boldsymbol\beta - \mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{y})$ 为零得到。特征共线时失效或不稳定；特征很多时代价高（$O(D^3)$）。

items.en: **Maximum likelihood:** least squares = MLE with independent Gaussian noise of constant variance; MAE would be Laplace noise; ridge a Gaussian prior.
items.zh: **最大似然：**最小二乘 = 独立、方差恒定的高斯噪声下的 MLE；MAE 对应拉普拉斯噪声；岭回归对应高斯先验。

items.en: **Gradient descent:** $\beta_j \leftarrow \beta_j + \frac{2\eta}{n}\sum_i \varepsilon_i x_{ij}$. Learning rate: too small is slow, too large diverges. Standardise features.
items.zh: **梯度下降：**$\beta_j \leftarrow \beta_j + \frac{2\eta}{n}\sum_i \varepsilon_i x_{ij}$。学习率：太小慢，太大发散。要标准化特征。

items.en: **Pros/cons:** interpretable, simple, exact; but linear only, collinearity, outliers, extrapolation.
items.zh: **优缺点：**可解释、简单、有精确解；但只能线性，怕共线性、离群点和外推。
